clauses.text:
6.6.
The disclosure and supply of the Confidential Information shall, in any case or for
any reason whatsoever, not cause transfer of ownership of such information and
assignment of Intellectual Property Rights in connection with the same.

risk.explanation_hint: 'Intellectual Property' clause — moderate risk — risky language: unlimited-scope — classifier and reference-bank disagree

explanation.text: This clause is risky because it uses "unlimited-scope" language ("in any case or for any reason whatsoever") to completely block any transfer of intellectual property (IP) or ownership. In standard business agreements, parties often need to transfer or license IP rights to collaborate effectively or deliver final products. Under this strict wording, you are prevented from acquiring any IP rights under the contract, even if you fully pay for them or if the transfer is necessary for the project.
explanation.suggested_action: Negotiate to remove the phrase "in any case or for any reason whatsoever" and add a specific exception for IP that is meant to be transferred or licensed to you as part of the project deliverables. You should also define exactly what "Confidential Information" is being shared so this restriction does not accidentally apply to your own IP.

clauses.text:
7. Intellectual Property Rights

All Intellectual Property Rights comprised in any and all materials (including software,
source code, documentation, data, concepts and ideas) or any part thereof created or
developed (whether jointly or independently by either Party) during the term of the
Agreement (collectively, the “Data”) shall, unless otherwise expressly agreed between the
Parties, be deemed to be irrevocably assigned to and shall vest in the Company upon
creation without further charge. If required by the Company, Consultant shall do all things
and sign all documents necessary to vest all such Intellectual property Rights assigned or
otherwise transferred or granted to the Company under this Agreement.

8. Termination

risk.explanation_hint: 'Intellectual Property' clause — HIGH RISK — risky language: unlimited-scope, irrevocable, assignment — score floored by substantive-risk override (high)

explanation.text: This clause is highly risky because it forces you to "irrevocably assign" (permanently give away) all intellectual property created during the contract, even if you developed it independently. It covers an overly broad scope of materials, including your "concepts and ideas," which means you lose ownership of your own thoughts and background methods. Standard practice is for a consultant to retain ownership of their pre-existing tools and ideas, while only transferring ownership of the specific, final deliverables paid for by the client.
explanation.suggested_action: Propose revising this clause to state that you retain ownership of your pre-existing intellectual property and general concepts, and that ownership of new materials only transfers to the Company upon written agreement and full payment for the services. You should also narrow the definition of "Data" to include only final, specific deliverables rather than broad "ideas" or "software."
